label: Early original-phase input (step 1-2) of w/s/t/e/c/v/f, boosted when the sequence starts with y/h/1/x/0/g/u/e/m
explanation: Almost all of its activation (98.5%) falls in the original phase, at steps 1-3. Step 2 alone holds 73% of the mass and step 1 holds 20%. It never fires at step 0, and it is essentially silent at the delimiter and during copying (1.4% of mass). Which token is input matters most: w is strongest (8x lift, 28% of mass), followed by s, t, e, c, v and f. The prefix also matters. Activation is higher when the first token is y/h/1/x/0/g, and the strongest examples (y u w, y e w, h u w) pair input w at step 2 with prev_tok u/e and first token y/h. The unit behaves like a conjunctive code over the first 2-3 tokens. Restricting to steps 1-2 and the w/s/t/e/c/v/f set gives recall 0.78 and mass recall 0.83, but precision is only 0.22. Adding the first-token condition raises precision to 0.46 with recall 0.49 (dev F1 0.47). No simple predicate captures the exact token combinations. It does not fire on b/n/j/u inputs, on step 0, or later in the sequence.
